messages.subject: Measuring duration and pauses between very short signals with timer function
messages.subject_clean: Measuring duration and pauses between very short signals with timer function
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I am trying to measure the duration of the notes of a call and the pauses between the notes (spectrogram attached). However, the notes are very short (0.001-0.003 s) and the amplitude of the notes raises throughout the call. It is really difficult to segregate the signal from the noise, because the inicial notes have small amplitudes. I thought maybe a good solution would be to  restrict the frequency or to use the length of the pauses to try to target only the signal, but neither are possible with timer function. I am using the following parameters:

temp_param <- timer (som, f = 44100, threshold = 5, dmin=0.001, msmooth = c(64,75))

Any ideas? Thank you very much!

Me. Pedro P. G. Taucce

messages.subject_clean: [seewave] Spectrogram scale is changed after filtering with fir()
messages.body_plain:
Dear Molly,

I do not know what was the sampling frequency of your object a but you specify f=6262 when plotting the spectrogram of b.
a and b should have the sample sampling frequency.
You might use output="Wave" to be sure to save the sampling frequeny.

This test seems to work:

data(tico)
spectro(tico)
filter <- fir(tico, from=4000, output="Wave")
spectro(filter)

HTH

Jerome

messages.body_plain:
Hi Julia,

I think your best bet is to use a combo of layout() and plotting the frequency spectrum by hand. If you check out a conversation Martin and I had a couple of weeks ago, we go over how to extract spectrum data and plot it by hand (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/seewave/_69Stm_gTtc).

You can then use plot(x = , y = , etc.) to plot the axes as you want them. I would play around with the layout() function to group the three plots together (http://www.statmethods.net/advgraphs/layout.html).

If you're comfortable with R, there are also ways of extracting data from all three of the plots and plotting them with ggplot2 and grid.arrange. However, spectrograms in ggplot2 can be extremely computationally challenging in my experience! I usually have to downsample them first.

Good luck and let us know how it goes,

Steffi

par(mar=c(0,4.5,1,0))
spectro(tico, scale=FALSE, tlab="", axisX=FALSE, yaxt="n", cex.lab=1.2)
par(mar=c(0,0,1,1))
meanspec(tico, plot=2, flab="")

messages.body_plain:
Hi Juliana,

I think the problem you have is that you're opening a file with SoX, but are not telling SoX what to do with that file. In a simple case, Sox takes commands in the following format:

input output effect

For example, if you wanted to trim the file you should something like this (I've shortened your file paths for clarity):

library(seewave)
sox("inteiro34m.wav inteiro34m_clip.wav trim 0.25 0.75")

Where inteiro34m.wav is the input file, inteiro34m_clip.wav is the new output file and trim 0.25, 0.75 is the effect you want to apply (you can string multiple effects together).

Or try:

sox("inteiro34m.wav", exe = "play")

If this still produces an error, try walking yourself through the examples in ?sox. They should work and if they don't, we'll have a better idea of where your problems are.

Good luck!

Steffi
